title: objectql: the 503 ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE text for a failed datasource always blames a startup connect under OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE, which is false for an install-time or Setup-created datasource
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

## Finding

`DatasourceUnavailableError` (`packages/objectql/src/driver-connect-errors.ts`, the non-`remote`, non-`blocked` arm, ~L268-271 on `main` 549203d0) explains every failed datasource the same way:

> it failed to connect at startup and the server was started with `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE`. Nothing re-runs the connect — the server must be restarted once the datasource is reachable.

That is true only for a code datasource whose boot connect failed under that flag. It is false for:

- a datasource declared by a package installed into a running runtime (`POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local`), whose connect fails at install time with no flag involved (PR #28132, #28039, measured by its card thread: a bound read answers this 503 for an unresolved credential);
- a datasource created in Setup whose connect failed.

The message then tells an operator to restart a server that was never started with the flag, and names a cause that did not happen.

## Expected

The text names the cause the connection service actually retained for that datasource (or a neutral "failed to connect; see Setup → Datasources"), and says "restart" only where a restart is what re-runs the connect.

## Scope

`packages/objectql/src/driver-connect-errors.ts` and its pins. No new error code; the 503 and `ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` stay. Found while reviewing PR #28132; not in that PR's scope.
